remarks_1999: Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate work was exhibited in 1933 New York (An American Place) exhibition as "no. 3. 'Barn No. 1.'" Four barn paintings appear on the checklist: no. 3, "Barn No. 1", no. 7, "Barn No. 2", no. 12, "Little Barn", and no. 14, "White Barn No. 3." See Appendix III, figure 53. No. 3, "Barn No. 1" follows no. 2 on the checklist, "White Flower No. 1," and precedes no. 4, "White Calla Lily." The checklist reflects the order on the walls as shown in the installation photographs, see Appendix III, figures 53, 54. The painting listed as no. 3, "Barn No. 1" is "White Barn with Red Door," see cat. no. 806. This work, cat. no. 807 or cat. no. 808 was possibly no. 14, "White Barn No. 3" on the checklist. See cat. nos. 805–8. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.title: Stables

description: Two white stable buildings fill the frame: a small structure stands on left side of the canvas and a larger one on the right. Both have pitched burgundy roofs and dark gray doors. Stretching below the buildings is an expanse of green grass. Above the buildings is a sky full of fluffy white clouds.
